title: Option leverage by strike: why a 50% strike gives about 2x
summary: Using a three-month option on a $100 stock, the speaker shows that extrinsic value peaks at the money and leverage rises as the strike moves out of the money: about 10x at the money and 20 to 30x far out of the money. For stock replacement he uses a deep in-the-money call at about 50% of the stock price, which gives about 2x leverage.

steps.caption: The at-the-money call is almost all extrinsic value. Its leverage is about 10x.
The $50 strike call is mostly intrinsic value. Its leverage is about 2x.
Far out-of-the-money calls reach 20 to 30x leverage, like lottery tickets.
The deep ITM call breaks even close to the stock price, so it tracks the stock with less capital.

takeaways: Extrinsic value peaks at the money.
Leverage rises as the strike moves out of the money: about 10x ATM, 20-30x far OTM.
For stock replacement the speaker uses a strike near 50% of the stock price for about 2x leverage.
caveats: The calculator in the video is the speaker's own tool.
Leverage figures are approximate and change with volatility and time.
